Subject: Onsite lead capture: QR form + HubSpot mapping

Hi team,

We're lining up lead capture for Redwood's booth at CloudSummit (Aug 18-20) and want to land on a QR-first flow that posts clean contact + consent data into HubSpot in real-time. Key asks: 

- Can LeadCapture provide a lightweight QR web form (hosted or iframe) that returns a small payload we can map to HubSpot? We prefer POST to a webhook or direct CRM integration.
- Required fields we need: first_name, last_name, email, company, role, country, event_source, session_id. Optional: notes, product_interest (multi-select), consent_timestamp, consent_text.
- Must include explicit EU/US consent language option and a checkbox with the text we can customize. Can you share your current default consent copy and whether you support per-region text?
- Is the device scanning the QR allowed to cache drafts (we prefer no PII cached on kiosk devices) and do you offer a kiosk mode that wipes after sync?

Marissa: can you review the field list and add any HubSpot property names you'd like us to pre-create?
Dylan: looping you for partner-side API key / billing considerations.

If you can send an integration spec and sample payload, we'll get our Sales Ops to map HubSpot properties and open the ticket.

Thanks,

Ava Chen
Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the details — happy to support. Quick answers up front, and I attached our API spec and a sample XLS with suggested field-to-CRM mappings. See attachments: LeadCapture-API-spec.pdf, onsite-form-specs.xlsx, onsite-qr-sample.png.

Summary:
- We provide a hosted responsive QR form and a kiosk mode. Kiosk mode is configured to clear local storage on session end; no PII is retained on-device longer than 15 seconds after successful POST.
- Integration options: webhook POST (recommended) or native HubSpot connector. For webhook mode, the payload is JSON (fields below). We can sign requests with HMAC or a short-lived API key.
- Sample payload (JSON): {"first_name":"Jane","last_name":"Doe","email":"jane.doe@example.com","company":"Acme Payments","role":"Head of Ops","country":"US","event_source":"CloudSummit Booth D12","session_id":"sess_789","product_interest":["Embeddings","Hosted API"],"consent_timestamp":"2025-08-18T10:14:00Z","consent_text":"I consent to Redwood Inference processing my data as described."}

Consent: we support per-region copy and a checkbox boolean in payload (consent_given: true/false). We'll include consent_text in the payload so you can persist the exact language used.

Security: we support signed webhooks (HMAC-SHA256) and IP allowlists. We also provide a one-time API key to configure the kiosk devices.

Next steps:
1) Confirm desired HubSpot property names for required fields.
2) Decide webhook vs native connector (webhook gives more control and faster onboarding).
3) We'll provision a staging API key and send a test event.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week if you want to walk through the mapping.

Best,
Tom Reyes
LeadCapture Integrations
ops@leadcapture.com
+1 (206) 555-0110

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-08-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite lead capture: QR form + HubSpot mapping

Thanks Tom — that payload looks good. Quick mapping proposal for Sales Ops and HubSpot: 

- first_name -> hs_firstname (single-line text)
- last_name -> hs_lastname (single-line text)
- email -> email (contact identifier)
- company -> company (company name)
- role -> jobtitle
- country -> country
- event_source -> recent_conversion_source (create custom property)
- session_id -> lead_session_id (hidden text)
- product_interest -> product_interest (multi-checkbox)
- consent_timestamp -> consent_timestamp (date/time)
- consent_text -> consent_text (multi-line)
- notes -> description

Consent language (proposed):
"By providing my contact information, I consent to Redwood Inference storing and processing my data for follow-up communications about Redwood products and services. For information on data processing, see https://redwood.ai/privacy."

I also recommend adding a hidden property for "event_campaign" with value "CloudSummit 2025" so we can attribute pipeline.

Action items:
- Rachel: can you open a HubSpot ticket to create the custom properties above and confirm API permissions for the webhook user? (HS-4821 is fine if you want to reuse the ticket).
- Ava: if you approve the consent text above, I'll add it to the mapping doc and send to Tom for confirmation.

A quick note on opt-ins: legal asked that we batch email sends for new contacts (send nurture after 24 hours) rather than immediate sequences for EU leads — worth flagging in the mapping.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Events Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.com
